Article Title: 'Govt cremated body forcibly': Gulzar Singh's family alleges last rites conducted without consent
Article Text:
'Administration cremated the body forcibly, without our consent,' says Gulzar Singh's son.

NEW DELHI: The family of Gulzar Singh, a Dalit labourer from Punjab’s Sangrur district who died by suicide after allegedly facing harassment, has accused the "government of forcibly cremating his body without their consent. "Gulzar’s son Lakhwinder Singh alleged that the family was not allowed to see his father’s face before the last rites and that they did not receive his clothes or other belongings.Speaking to ANI on Thursday, Lakhwinder said, "The govt cremated the body forcibly, without our consent. We should get justice. Cheema sahib should be jailed."He also alleged that the government had promised the family a job and other assistance but failed to provide them."The government forcibly carried out the last rites. They told us they would provide a job and other things, but we received nothing. I was in a state of depression. The police pressure was immense; it was the district police. Yes, it happened without our consent. Didn't even let me see his face. Don't even get his clothes. I demand justice," he added.Earlier on Thursday, National Commission for Scheduled Castes chairman Kishor Makwana met Gulzar’s family.Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old member of the Valmiki community from Dirba in Sangrur district, died on Monday night after allegedly consuming poison.His family alleged that he was harassed, intimidated and subjected to caste-based abuse after he questioned Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema about the drug menace during a public meeting in Toor Banjara village on September 6.A purported video of Gulzar’s final statement shows him raising concerns with Cheema about the availability of ‘chitta’ in the area and saying his own son was also addicted to drugs.According to his family, police and local panchayat members allegedly pressured him to apologise after the incident. They claimed that some people also subjected him to caste-based abuse and asked him to appear before the village panchayat.Gulzar consumed poison around noon on Monday and was taken to hospitals in Sangrur and Patiala before being shifted to DMC Hospital in Ludhiana, where he died later that night.Police registered an FIR against five residents of Toor Banjara — Baljeet Singh, Sukhdev Singh, Vicky Singh, Gona Singh and Baljinder Kaur — under Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for abetment to suicide and provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.The accused include the village sarpanch and her husband, according to the allegations. The sarpanch’s husband has denied the charges, saying the allegations against the panchayat were baseless.Dirba SHO Gurvinder Singh said further action would be based on medical and investigative findings.The case also triggered a political row in Punjab, with the BJP and Congress demanding action against Cheema and an independent probe.BJP leader Amit Malviya alleged that Gulzar was pressured by local AAP-linked village leaders after questioning Cheema over the drug menace.“Raising the issue of Punjab’s drug menace should not cost a citizen his life. Gulzar Singh, a resident of Toor Banjara village in the Dirba constituency, reportedly questioned AAP Minister Harpal Singh Cheema during his visit about the unchecked sale of “chitta”, saying that his own son was battling addiction and had sold off the family’s belongings. What followed, was pressure and harassment by local AAP-linked village leaders, who demanded that Gulzar Singh apologise for questioning the minister. He refused," Malviya said."In a video recorded before consuming poison, Gulzar Singh held four people responsible for his plight, including Harpal Cheema and local village leaders. He later died despite treatment. This is deeply disturbing. A government that cannot tolerate questions on the drug menace and intimidates a citizen for raising them has a serious case to answer. Punjab deserves accountability, not intimidation," he added.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also attacked the AAP government, demanding that chief minister Bhagwant Mann seek Cheema’s resignation and ensure an independent investigation."A dangerous pattern is emerging under Punjab's AAP government - if you question government's failures, the response will come in the form of threats and torture," Rahul said."Gulzar Singh ji, from the Dalit community, who had to watch his son fall victim to drugs, asked the Finance Minister just this much: why has the government failed so miserably in stopping the drug trade? For just this, he was tortured and humiliated so much, pressured so intensely to apologize, that he consumed poison," he said.The government's job is to answer to the people, not to "trample upon" those who ask questions, he added.The AAP has accused the opposition of “vulture politics” and of trying to politically exploit the family’s grief. AAP media in-charge Baltej Pannu said, “Wherever someone dies by suicide or wherever a dead body is found, they reach there and try to bake political bread over the funeral pyre.”
Article Summary: Gulzar Singh, a Dalit labourer from Sangrur district, died on Monday night after allegedly consuming poison. His family alleged that he was harassed, intimidated and subjected to caste-based abuse after he questioned Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema about the drug menace.

Article Title: 'They would kick us': Stalin takes on Vijay over 'jaw gesture', recalls Emergency-era prison days
Article Text:
His remarks came after Vijay launched a strong attack on the DMK in the assembly

NEW DELHI: DMK president MK Stalin on Thursday hit back at Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay over his recent remarks in the state assembly, accusing him of attempting to demean the party and its leaders while recalling his arrest and alleged custodial torture during the Emergency.Responding to Vijay’s criticism of the DMK, Stalin said the party’s history and its ideological struggle could not be changed by political attacks.“Thambi Vijay, what you said is true. It is not a lie. During the Emergency, opposing it, leader Kalaignar organized a huge gathering at the Marina beach and severely criticized the MISA Act,” Stalin said in a video message shared on X.His remarks came after Vijay launched a strong attack on the DMK in the assembly on Wednesday, accusing previous governments of corruption and referring to the Sarkaria Commission as well as Enforcement Directorate documents concerning alleged corruption during the 2021-26 regime.Stalin recalled that the Union government dismissed the DMK government on January 31, 1976, during the Emergency imposed by the Indira Gandhi government.“The very next second after dismissing the government, police came to the Gopalapuram house to arrest me under the MISA Act,” Stalin said, recounting how his father and former chief minister M Karunanidhi told police that his son was away campaigning and would return the next day.Stalin said that after he returned, Karunanidhi himself called the police and asked them to arrest him.Recalling his time in prison, Stalin alleged that he was subjected to severe physical abuse and was kept with other prisoners in a small room where leprosy patients had earlier been housed.“In prison, many atrocities happened to me. We were taken and locked up in a place where leprosy patients were kept. Ten people were locked inside a small room. Inside that same room, in a single pot, all of us had to urinate,” he said.Stalin alleged that police beat prisoners with lathis at night, kicked them with boots and that other inmates also assaulted them. He recalled the death of DMK leader and former MP Chitti Babu, whom he said died in jail following the beatings.“Due to their beating, my dear brother, Member of Parliament Chitti Babu, died inside the jail itself. Due to their beating, my jawbone was broken,” Stalin said.The DMK has condemned Vijay’s remarks and announced a statewide protest on September 12, accusing the chief minister of making “scurrilous remarks” against Stalin, Karunanidhi and other party leaders.Law minister R Nirmal Kumar, however, has disputed Stalin’s account, saying there was no official record to indicate that his detention during the Emergency was under MISA. The minister said Stalin was arrested following remarks concerning Indira Gandhi and her 20-point programme.Stalin also rejected Vijay’s allegations relating to the Sarkaria Commission and corruption charges against Karunanidhi, arguing that successive governments would have acted if the allegations had been established.Turning to Vijay’s conduct in the Assembly, Stalin urged him to maintain the dignity expected of a chief minister and focus on governance rather than political controversies.“The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly has dignity and respect. It is a place sculpted by many great leaders, great men. That responsibility is now with you,” Stalin said.
Article Summary: DMK president MK Stalin hit back at Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay over his recent remarks. He accused Vijay of attempting to demean the party and its leaders while recalling his arrest and alleged custodial torture during the Emergency. Vijay launched a strong attack on the DMK in the assembly on Wednesday.

Article Title: NC tells Congress: Full Vande Mataram a constitutional duty
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: National Conference fired a political broadside at ally Congress Wednesday, defending full renditions of Vande Mataram at govt functions in J&K as a “constitutional” duty.Congress objected after all six stanzas of the national song was played at the inauguration of J&K’s first international film festival in Srinagar attended by CM Omar Abdullah and NC president Farooq Abdullah on Sept 7. As at other official functions, Omar stood at attention throughout.J&K Congress president Tariq Hamid Karra said NC and Congress should respect how the song’s place in India’s national life evolved through both the freedom movement and constitutional journey. “National symbols, songs and traditions occupy a special place in the heart of every Indian. Their true strength lies in their ability to bind together a nation as diverse as ours,” he said, calling it a concern that alliance partners had chosen to sing the full version.NC countered, asking Congress to look at CMs of states governed by the party, including Telangana and Karnataka, who have participated in full renditions.NC chief spokesperson Tanvir Sadiq shared on X a video featuring Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar at an event where the unabridged song was sung. He said govt protocol must be separated from party ideology. “NC has a clear stand. When Parliament has adopted it, playing Vande Mataram becomes a statutory obligation and that is what govt did,” Sadiq said.CM Omar later shared Sadiq’s statements on X.A Union home ministry protocol directive in Feb mandated the six-stanza version of the song at all state functions, official events and legislature sessions. In Aug, the President cleared Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, which puts Vande Mataram on a par with the national anthem, making disrespect/disruption a punishable offence. The amended law did not change the stanzas, but people are now obligated to respect Vande Mataram as a constitutional duty.NC spokesperson Imran Nabi Dar said: “This is a constitutional obligation, and every one holding a constitutional office has to accept it, whether it is the CM, an MP or anyone else,” he said, adding the full version is now regularly played at govt functions across J&K.Dar acknowledged the objection among Muslims. “Though religiously it is not acceptable to Muslims, it is a constitutional obligation that has to be fulfilled,” he said.The freedom movement broadly adopted first two stanzas of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay’s 1875 poem, while the full song has six containing religious imagery that has drawn objections from Muslims. Congress general secretary GA Mir said freedom fighters had shaped the version used by the movement with inclusivity in mind.(inputs from PTI)
Article Summary: Congress objected after all six stanzas of the national song was played at the inauguration of J&K’s first international film festival in Srinagar. NC countered, asking Congress to look at CMs of states governed by the party, including Telangana and Karnataka.

Article Title: ‘Wanted to teach him a lesson’: Accused on assault that killed Manipuri musician
Article Text:
Accused wanted to ‘teach him a lesson’, police say

Police examine racial angle, dhaba owner’s role

Singh died hours after assault

Northeast body seeks swift, impartial probe

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Who was Chongtham Vikram Singh?

NEW DELHI: The men accused of killing Manipuri musician Chongtham Vikram Singh in southeast Delhi allegedly wanted to “teach him a lesson” for objecting to noise outside his home, but did not expect the assault to turn fatal, police said on Wednesday.During questioning, the accused allegedly told police that they assaulted the 54-year-old musician with fists and blows after he objected to the commotion outside his residence in Kilokari, according to the police, as cited by news agency PTI.Singh had on some occasions complained to the owner of a nearby dhaba about the noise caused by people gathering there, a senior police officer said. However, police had not received any formal complaint from Singh regarding the noise.The dhaba remained open until around midnight and attracted customers from neighbouring areas as well as students living nearby, police said.Police said they were examining all aspects of the case, including whether there was any racial angle. So far, the investigation has not revealed any instance of a racial slur being used against Singh during the altercation, a police source said.The FIR registered at Sunlight Colony police station on the complaint of Singh's son mentions Section 103(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, pertaining to group murder in circumstances covered by the provision.Police are awaiting the post-mortem report to ascertain the exact nature of the injuries sustained by Singh. Prima facie, he appears to have suffered internal injuries that led to his death.The police are also examining the role of the dhaba owner and its operations. So far, no irregularity in the functioning of the establishment has come to light, sources said. Action would be taken against the owner if anything emerges during the investigation.CCTV footage is being scrutinised and witnesses are being questioned to establish the sequence of events and the circumstances that led to the assault.The incident took place around 11.30 pm on Sunday when Singh went downstairs after hearing a commotion outside his home.According to the complaint, when his son heard his father shouting, he opened the door and saw a group of men kicking and punching him.Singh subsequently returned upstairs but complained of breathlessness. His 20-year-old son Yaiphaba took him to Holy Family Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries around 6 am the following day, police said.Seven men have been arrested and a juvenile apprehended in connection with the case. The accused have been identified as Bharat Kumar, 19, Pramod, 26, Ramzan Khan, 22, Deepanshu, 21, Mohan Vishwakarma, 32, Vijay, 36, and Mannu, 26.The killing has sparked concern among members of Delhi's northeastern community, with several residents alleging that people from the region face racial slurs and discrimination in the national capital.The North Eastern Students' Organisation (NESO) on Wednesday condemned Singh's killing and demanded a swift and impartial probe.NESO chairman Samuel B Jyrwa said the incident was deeply disturbing and called for all those responsible to be brought to justice.“It is deeply disturbing that a person can lose his life merely for raising an objection to disturbance outside his own home. We demand a transparent and impartial investigation and exemplary punishment for every person found responsible,” Jyrwa said in a statement, as cited by PTI.Jyrwa said the killing could not be viewed in isolation from what he described as continuing harassment, racial discrimination, stereotyping, intimidation and violence faced by people from the Northeast in different parts of mainland India.“For years, Northeastern citizens living, studying and working outside the region have repeatedly reported being subjected to racial slurs, verbal abuse, physical attacks, social discrimination and other forms of humiliation because of their appearance, identity and place of origin,” he alleged.NESO urged authorities to treat the matter with seriousness and urgency and ensure that nobody responsible for the crime evades accountability.“The law must be applied firmly and equally, irrespective of the identity or background of the perpetrators,” Jyrwa said.The organisation also called for stronger preventive measures, effective enforcement of the law, sensitisation of police and public institutions, and mechanisms to ensure the safety and dignity of people from the Northeast.“The loss of Chongtham Vikram Singh is not merely a personal tragedy for his family and loved ones, but a matter of deep concern for the entire Northeastern community,” Jyrwa said.Singh had lived in Kilokari for more than two decades. He was a well-known musician and guitarist, and had been the lead guitarist of the Manipur rock band Phoenix in the early 1980s.He later worked as a music teacher and performer in Delhi.NESO expressed solidarity with Singh's family and the people of Manipur and demanded justice for him and accountability for everyone found responsible for his death.
Article Summary: Chongtham Vikram Singh, 54, died hours after being assaulted outside his home. Seven men have been arrested and a juvenile apprehended in connection with the case. North Eastern Students' Organisation (NESO) condemns Singh's killing and demands a swift and impartial probe.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister and TVK chief C Joseph Vijay on Wednesday named his alliance with the Congress, VCK, MDMK and IUML the “Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance” as leaders of the parties met for the second time at the TVK headquarters in Chennai.TVK sources cited by news agency PTI had earlier confirmed that key alliance partners, including the Congress, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK), Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), and Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (MDMK), would participate in the meeting.However, the CPM and CPI have decided to skip the meeting, marking their second consecutive boycott of formal alliance talks since July 1.Explaining the decision, CPM state secretary P Shanmugam said on Tuesday that the Left parties’ outside support would remain strictly issue-based, with the aim of maintaining stability in the Assembly.Adding to the tensions is a growing public rift between the TVK and the Congress over the question of national leadership.Statements from TVK legislators and ministers projecting chief minister Vijay as a potential Prime Ministerial candidate for the 2029 general elections have drawn strong opposition from Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) leaders.Congress minister S Rajesh Kumar has firmly asserted that Rahul Gandhi remains the undisputed leader of the national opposition bloc. Article Title: Creating a multi-layered security grid in Delhi, one Brics at a time
Article Text:
Creating a multi-layered security grid in Delhi, one Brics at a time

NEW DELHI: When the 'Flying Kremlin' and other ultra-secure aircraft touch down in Delhi this weekend, they won't just bring Russian President Vladimir Putin and other high-profile world leaders to the Brics Summit, they will land with a fully autonomous fortress-on-wheels featuring personal food-testing labs, decoy dignitaries and armoured limousines built to survive landmines and chemical attacks.As Delhi transforms into an impenetrable, multi-layered defensive grid, security personnel are bracing for a high-stakes security operation where AI-aimed snipers scan rooftops, gesture-recognition cameras spot human posture shifts, commandos slither down ropes from hovering helicopters and anti-graffiti strike teams patrol the streets 24/7, guarding against everything from high-tech threats to stealth protest tactics.The capital, sources said, hasn't seen security this tight since the 2023 G20 summit, and preparations this time are even more extensive. Unmanned aerial vehicles have been categorised as one of the most potent threats, and systems that can jam drone signals or shoot them down have been installed at several locations.Every dignitary or their hotel or carcade has been assigned a code name or call sign to ensure they are guided smoothly between locations without any overlap or security glitches.Intelligence inputs have hinted at the possibility of flash protests and spray-painting of inflammatory slogans near the venues, targeting some foreign leaders. Cops have formed anti-graffiti teams for round-the-clock patrolling to thwart any such attempts.President Putin's security grid comprises a sophisticated protective shield managed jointly by Russia's Federal Protective Service (FSO) and Indian counter-terrorism forces. Ground mobility will be centred around his custom-made, heavily armoured Aurus Senat limousine, often referred to as a "rolling bunker". Transported directly from Moscow, the state car is built to withstand chemical attacks, landmines and sniper fire, complete with run-flat tyres and an independent emergency oxygen supply.Up in the air, the Russian leader travels in a specially modified Ilyushin IL-96-300PU aircraft, known as the "Flying Kremlin", which operates alongside decoy jets, advanced missile-defence countermeasures and secure command systems. On the ground, the innermost protective layer comprises elite officers from Russian Presidential Security Service (SBP), supported by advanced FSO teams that sanitise every scheduled and potential itinerary venue. The Russian delegation manages its own strict logistics, travelling with personal chefs, portable testing laboratories for food and drink, and measures to collect biological waste, alongside deploying dummy dignitaries in select hotels to boost operational security.Securing the designated summit hotels in central Delhi, Aerocity and Gurgaon presented one of the most formidable logistical challenges for intelligence and law enforcement agencies. Every hotel is being managed as an independent secure zone under its assigned DCP venue commander, supervised by special commissioner-rank officers overseeing broader zones.Within each hotel, two rooms have been repurposed into operational command posts: a primary security control room linked directly to Delhi Police's central C4i command node and a secondary contingency room dedicated to emergency management.To prevent unauthorised access, advanced AI cameras equipped with posture-detection and intrusion-alert software monitor perimeter walls and hallways, capable of flagging unusual physical movements like crawling or wall-scaling. Hotel staff have undergone rigorous multi-round background checks conducted by special branch and special cell, with movement restricted strictly to assigned floors using specially programmed digital keycards.
Article Summary: The capital hasn't seen security this tight since the 2023 G20 summit. AI-aimed snipers scan rooftops, gesture-recognition cameras spot human posture shifts. Unmanned aerial vehicles have been categorised as one of the most potent threats.

Article Title: 'Rahul mian' can't grasp Vande importance: Nitin Nabin
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A day after Congress took exception to J&K CM Omar Abdullah and his father Farooq Abdullah standing during the full rendition of Vande Mataram BJP on Wednesday attacked Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for opposing the full version of the national song and dubbed him "Rahul mian".BJP president Nitin Nabin targeted the main opposition party at a presser in Delhi and stepped up his attack at a BJP event in Haldwani in Uttarakhand. BJP has said Congress's stand is driven by its appeasement of Muslim voters, a section of which considers Vande Mataram idolatrous in violation of their religious beliefs.Congress general secretary K C Venugopal Tuesday said on social media, "With respect and humility, we would like our allies to honour the wisdom and judgment of our freedom fighters, and stand with us in singing only the version of this beautiful and historic song that they adopted. That version was chosen deliberately, to keep the song from being communalised-a threat as real today as it was then."Blaming Rahul for Congress's stand on Vande Mataram, Nabin said Rahul cannot appreciate the national song's significance as he was raised in a "foreign culture". He is unable to grasp the importance of Indian culture, the BJP chief alleged.Such a Congress must be brought to an end, he told BJP members, ruing that a song that inspired freedom fighters to make the ultimate sacrifice makes the opposition party and its former president Sonia Gandhi feel "embarrassed".It was a reference to Sonia gesturing to Congress members at an Independence Day event at the party's office when the song was being played in full.Nabin said an "anti-national and anarchic" mindset is driving Congress. BJP said the Srinagar event has confirmed Congress' isolation within its own alliance and its emergence as the new Muslim League.The song has become a symbol of the honour and unity of nation, he asserted.
Article Summary: BJP president Nitin Nabin targeted the main opposition party at a presser in Delhi. He stepped up his attack at a BJP event in Haldwani in Uttarakhand. Nabin said Rahul cannot appreciate the national song's significance as he was raised in a "foreign culture"

Article Title: Ladakh groups claim breakthrough in talks with MHA on legislative powers
Article Text:
Ladakh groups claim breakthrough in talks with MHA on legislative powers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance, the two organisations negotiating with the Union govt for administrative autonomy to Ladakh under the Sixth Schedule, claimed a breakthrough Wednesday in talks with the MHA’s subcommittee in Delhi on legislative powers over land, culture and language, forests and natural resources.In a joint statement, the groups said the meeting furthered the “in-principle understanding” reached during talks on May 22 and July 3 on Ladakh’s demands, including constitutional safeguards through special provisions under Article 371.They said MHA stopped short of guaranteeing powers across the board under Lists II and III of the Seventh Schedule, including law and order.MHA assured compensation to the families of those killed and the protesters injured in the Sept 24, 2025, violence in Leh, the groups claimed. The Union govt also agreed to withdraw cases against 24 people and review those against another 34 on a case-to-case basis. Cases against 25 people have already been withdrawn.Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra wrote on X about the “general air of positivity” at the Delhi meeting without elaborating beyond the agenda. “The broad contours of a sui generis model of governance under Article 371 were discussed. Deepening democracy is the goal,” he said.Another round of talks is scheduled for the first week of Oct.The groups said they were concerned over the formation of new districts, the creation of hill councils for each and what they called “major irreversible changes being done before an elected body at the Union Territory”.Making such changes before the UT body can legislate, they said, “would essentially deprive the people of Ladakh an opportunity to democratically decide on the structure of administration in Ladakh”.Ladakhi representatives have been in talks with MHA since 2023 for safeguards covering land, jobs, culture and environment. MHA set up the committee on Jan 2, 2023, but the process stalled after four people were killed and over 80 injured in alleged police firing on protesters demanding statehood in Leh in Sept last year.Activist Sonam Wangchuk , a LAB member, was accused of inciting the protesters, arrested and charged under the NSA. The Centre revoked his detention last March and he returned to the negotiating table in May.
Article Summary: Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance claim a breakthrough in talks with the MHA’s subcommittee in Delhi. The groups said the meeting furthered the “in- principle understanding’ reached during talks on May 22 and July 3. The Union govt also agreed to withdraw cases against 24 people and review those against another 34 on a case-to-case basis.

Article Title: ‘Pilot is a good leader’: Channi backs new Punjab Congress in-charge, says appointment brings ‘new hope’
Article Text:
File photo: Congress leaders Sachin Pilot and Charanjeet Singh Channi

Randhawa denies asking for Warring’s removal

Punjab Congress factionalism

Congress looks to restart Punjab outreach

NEW DELHI: Former Punjab chief minister and Congress leader Charanjit Singh Channi on Wednesday welcomed Sachin Pilot ’s appointment as the party’s general secretary in-charge of poll-bound Punjab, saying it had brought “new hope” among Congress workers in the state.Channi described Pilot as a “good leader” and said his appointment would benefit the party ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections.“The people of Punjab like Pilot, who comes from the neighbouring state. With his arrival (appointment as in-charge of Punjab), a new hope has arisen among Congress workers in Punjab and it will benefit us. A good leadership has come,” Channi told reporters in Delhi.Channi, Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa and Gurdaspur MLA Barindermeet Singh Pahra met Pilot in Delhi after he was given charge of Punjab.Channi expressed confidence that the Congress would form the next government in Punjab after the 2027 Assembly polls, which are due early next year.Asked whether Congress leaders would come together on one platform, Channi said the decisions being taken by the party leadership were creating a good atmosphere in favour of the Congress in Punjab.“Pilot is a good leader and he is capable of taking all of us along,” he said.The meeting came amid alleged factionalism within the Punjab Congress over the state leadership.When asked about the demand for changing Punjab Congress president Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, Randhawa rejected the suggestion that he or Channi had sought his removal.“When did we tell you that the PPCC president be changed? Did anyone ask about it? Do not say such a thing. Have Channi Saab or I or any leader asked about changing the PPCC,” said Randhawa, the former Punjab deputy chief minister and Gurdaspur MP.Channi also said the decision on the state Congress president was entirely with the party high command.“Who is to be made the president or in-charge, who is to be changed or who is not be changed, it is not in our hands. It is the decision of the party high command. What it decides, we go by it,” he said.The Congress on Saturday carried out a major organisational reshuffle and appointed Pilot as general secretary in-charge of Punjab, replacing Bhupesh Baghel.Pilot had until then been in charge of Chhattisgarh, where Baghel is a key leader and former chief minister. Baghel has now been assigned Assam, replacing Jitendra Singh.The differences within the Punjab Congress intensified after the party leadership on July 1 decided to retain Warring as the state unit chief and appoint Channi as chairperson of its campaign committee.A section of Congress leaders led by Channi opposed the decision to retain Warring and sought his removal.Channi’s supporters had openly demanded Warring’s removal as Punjab Congress chief and sought to have the Jalandhar MP declared the party’s chief ministerial face for the 2027 Assembly elections.Baghel’s recent visits to Punjab did not end the factionalism, while Channi’s supporters also accused him of “favouring” Warring.Warring had welcomed Pilot’s appointment and said there was no resentment among party leaders. He had expressed confidence that all leaders would come together to fight the elections.“There is no resentment. I think you will see that in the coming time, there may be some minor differences, but all of us, all the leaders, will come together on one platform and fight,” Warring had said.Warring had also described Pilot as a “national leader” and a “very dear colleague”, saying he was an “exceptionally hardworking and dynamic leader”.Senior Congress leader Raj Kumar Verka had also welcomed Pilot’s appointment, saying it would benefit the party and that Pilot’s experience and understanding of Punjab would help resolve the “minor mutual issues” within the state unit.The Congress is now looking to revive its organisational and electoral activities in Punjab ahead of the 2027 polls.The party is planning a statewide yatra in Punjab featuring Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, which could be held towards the end of September or in early October, subject to the festival calendar.The party had announced its election-related committees on July 1, but their functioning was affected by the subsequent differences within the state unit.With Pilot replacing Baghel as the Punjab in-charge, Congress leaders have publicly welcomed the change as the party prepares for the next Assembly election.
Article Summary: Former Punjab chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi welcomed Sachin Pilot ’s appointment as the party’s general secretary in-charge of poll-bound Punjab. NEW DELHI: A dispute has erupted over the ancestral home of Hindu saint Baba Neem Karoli Maharaj in Uttar Pradesh, with his six granddaughters alleging that the property is being illegally occupied and controlled by a trust headed by their aunt, PTI reported.Following the complaint, Firozabad District Magistrate Santosh Kumar Sharma has constituted a three-member committee to investigate the ownership and management of the property, according to PTI.The committee is headed by additional district magistrate (Judicial) Arvind Kumar Dwivedi and includes Tundla Sub-Divisional Magistrate Divya Singh and District Tourism Officer Vishal Srivastava.The dispute concerns house number 154 and adjoining structures in Akbarpur village under Tundla tehsil, the birthplace of Baba Neem Karoli, whose original name was Lakshmi Narayan Sharma, according to PTI.The property, which is being developed as a tourist attraction by the Uttar Pradesh tourism department, includes the saint's meditation room, dining area, guest quarters and bedroom.The ancestral residence is a duplex built on a plot measuring around 4,000 square feet and is currently managed by the Shri Neem Karoli Maharaj Trust, headed by the saint's daughter Girija Devi Bhatele. His late wife Rambeti was its former president.According to family sources cited by PTI, the dispute came to the fore during a family event on August 24, when the six daughters of the saint's late son Dharm Narayan Sharma were allegedly denied accommodation in rooms at the ancestral property.Following the incident, the six granddaughters, Sunita Sharma, Archana Sharma, Vandana Sharma, Bhavna Rawat, Ritu Tiwari and Richa Rawat, submitted a representation to the District Magistrate seeking that the ancestral residence be freed from the Trust's control, PTI reported.Manoj Rawat, husband of Bhavna Rawat, confirmed to PTI that relevant property documents had been submitted to the inquiry committee after it sought them.However, Dhananjay Sharma, son of the saint's other late son Anek Singh Sharma, rejected the allegations and said that the property had been handed over to the Trust in accordance with Baba Neem Karoli's wishes.He expressed concern over the public nature of the dispute and appealed to family members to resolve the matter amicably.Trust secretary Sanjay Gupta also denied allegations of illegal occupation and rejected claims of an internal dispute within the Trust. He said he had been appointed by Dharm Narayan Sharma and continued to serve the institution.Gupta told PTI that the Trust had not received any official notice from the district administration so far.The dispute comes amid renewed public interest in Baba Neem Karoli's life and legacy following the release of Hanuman Ansh, a devotional biographical film based on the saint's life.Released on August 7, 2026, the low-budget film starring Shobhinaww Satyaa became a sleeper hit following strong word-of-mouth publicity. It reportedly collected more than Rs 150 crore worldwide within a month, bringing renewed attention to the saint's life and his birthplace, PTI reported.
Article Summary: dispute erupts over ancestral home of Hindu saint Baba Neem Karoli Maharaj. Six granddaughters allege property is being illegally occupied and controlled by a trust headed by their aunt. Firozabad District Magistrate has constituted a three-member committee to investigate the ownership and management of the property.

Article Title: Supreme Court to examine marital rape exception under IPC, BNS
Article Text:
Supreme Court

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to examine whether the law excluding non-consensual sexual intercourse by a husband against his wife from the definition of rape can withstand constitutional scrutiny. The court is hearing challenges to the marital rape exception under both the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The issue came before a Bench hearing a batch of petitions challenging Exception 2 to Section 375 of the IPC. The pleas also question the corresponding exception under Section 63 of the BNS and seek its reading down to allow non-consensual sexual acts within marriage to be treated as rape.The Bench indicated that the matter involved a fundamental question about the limits of judicial interpretation, particularly whether courts can permit prosecution for conduct that Parliament has expressly excluded from the offence.The court also raised the question of whether an individual could be prosecuted for marital rape while the constitutional challenge to the statutory exception is yet to be decided.“We would definitely protect the victims but is it within the domain to prosecute a person where there is direct exclusion of a person under 375,” the court observed.The proceedings also covered an appeal arising from a March 2022 Karnataka high court ruling, which refused to quash rape charges against a husband accused of sexually assaulting his wife.Senior advocate Indira Jaising, appearing in the appeal, submitted that the Karnataka high court had held that prosecution could proceed where a wife was treated as a “sexual slave”. She also pointed to the subsequent raising of the age of consent from 16 to 18 years.Senior advocate Karuna Nundy argued that the constitutional challenge would require the court to consider whether the exception could be read down or interpreted in a manner consistent with constitutional guarantees.The Bench said the question before it was ultimately one of constitutional validity rather than social morality.“What is social morality? When people speak through their representatives - what we do is test it with the Constitution. It’s for the people to decide. Court says it can only speak its constitutional language,” the court observed.The Bench also made clear that it would not prejudge individual criminal proceedings while considering the larger constitutional challenge.“We don’t want to pronounce on that. We will take up constitutionality. We will examine the question,” the Court said.Counsel also raised questions about the BNS provisions relating to gang rape and the exception available to a husband.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Union government, said its counter-affidavit had already been filed. The court directed that it be circulated among all counsel within two days.The constitutional challenge will now be heard in detail on a date to be fixed.
Article Summary: The court is hearing challenges to the marital rape exception under both the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) The court also raised the question of whether an individual could be prosecuted for marital rape while the constitutional challenge to the statutory exception is yet to be decided.

The required details were subsequently filled in.According to the GBA, Rao was listed as a voter in Part No-129, Serial No-431 of the 76-Malleshwaram assembly constituency in the 2002 electoral roll.His name at the time was recorded as ‘Rama’.Explaining the discrepancy, the authority said the BLO decided against issuing a notice and instead recommended retaining Rao's name in the final roll."A discrepancy was noticed in the name of the Hon’ble person in the electoral roll. In view of this, the Booth Level Officer (BLO), without issuing any notice, has recommended inclusion of his name in the final electoral roll, considering him to be a respected person.Accordingly, necessary action has been initiated to include his name in the final electoral roll," the GBA said.He is currently enrolled as a voter in Part No-59, Serial No-187 of the 157-Malleshwaram assembly constituency under the name 'Prof CN Rao M'. The GBA said his name has consequently been included in the draft electoral roll.The clarification came after reports suggested that Rao had received a notice in connection with the electoral roll revision.
Article Summary: No notice was issued to Bharat Ratna awardee Prof C N R Rao over a discrepancy in his name in the electoral roll during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision. Article Title: 'Allies should stand with us': Congress calls out Abdullahs after full version of Vande Mataram played
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Congress has urged its allies to “stand with us” in singing a shorter version of Vande Mataram , after all six stanzas of the national song were played at an event attended by Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah and his father, Farooq Abdullah, the top two leaders of Congress ally National Conference (NC).Congress general secretary (organisation) KC Venugopal argued that the full version of Vande Mataram “sits uneasily with the syncretic and pluralist ethos that our freedom fighters envisioned and nurtured for India.”“For us, the considered judgment of Mahatma Gandhi, Pandit Nehru, Sardar Patel, Subhash Chandra Bose, Rajendra Prasad, Acharya Narendra Dev, Maulana Azad, Sarojini Naidu and J.B. Kripalani — shaped in no small part by the counsel of Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore — remains paramount,” Venugopal said on X.“With respect and humility, we would like our allies to honour the wisdom and judgment of our freedom fighters, and stand with us in singing only the version of this beautiful and historic song that they adopted,” he added.The Alappuzha MP maintained that the Congress' decision to sing only the first two stanzas was made “deliberately” to prevent the song from being “communalised." He was referring to the Congress’ 1937 resolution recommending that only the first two stanzas of the national song be sung to “maintain communal harmony."In July, the BJP-led Centre enacted the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, 2026, granting Vande Mataram statutory protection on par with the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana. The law mandates the singing of the full version at official events and provides for imprisonment of up to three years, a fine, or both for anyone found guilty of “insulting” the song.On August 15, Vande Mataram was played for the first time at the official Independence Day ceremony. It was played in full before and after Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s address to the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort in Delhi.Accused of "minority appeasement" by the ruling BJP, the Congress has stood its ground, repeatedly invoking the 1937 resolution to justify singing only the first two stanzas.
Article Summary: All six stanzas of the national song were played at an event attended by Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah and his father, Farooq Abdullah. The BJP-led Centre enacted the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, 2026, granting Vande Mataram statutory protection on par with the national anthem.

Article Title: DMK MLAs bundled out as row over Vijay’s remarks rocks Tamil Nadu assembly
Article Text:
Speaker JCD Prabhakar refused to accept DMK's demand to expunge CM Vijay's remark from assembly records

CHENNAI: DMK legislators were bundled out of the Tamil Nadu assembly on Tuesday after a stormy confrontation over chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s remarks on late chief minister M Karunanidhi, former Union minister Murasoli Maran, the Sarkaria Commission and ED dossiers relating to cases pending before courts.The dramatic scenes unfolded after speaker J C D Prabhakar refused to expunge Vijay’s remarks, prompting DMK members to raise slogans and staged a sit-in protest on the well of the House. As the protesting members refused to return to their seats despite repeated appeals, the speaker ordered marshals to remove them.The confrontation began during Zero Hour when DMK whip E V Velu raised objections to Vijay’s remarks made during his reply to the demands for grants for the home department on Monday. Velu accused the CM of making baseless allegations and referring to pending cases, saying this went against the traditions of the House.Referring to the Sarkaria Commission, Velu said late chief minister M G Ramachandran was the principal complainant but later told the commission that he had “no idea whatsoever” about the complaint and that it had been drafted by a party functionary, Kannan from Salem. “At the conclusion, Sarkaria made it clear that there was no prima facie case in all the 28 allegations.Therefore, there was no provision for filing any case,” Velu said.He referred to DK leader K Veeramani and Left leaders being booked under MISA, like DMK leader M K Stalin, and said Vijay’s remarks had demeaned their democratic struggle.Ministers Aadhav Arjuna and R Nirmalkumar defended the CM, saying Vijay had referred to the Sarkaria Commission report and other publicly available documents as part of his fight against corruption. They accused the DMK of being the “root of corruption.”Former minister Govi Chezhiaan then posed three questions to the treasury benches: whether the CM could cite ED dossiers as evidence when the cases were pending before courts? whether the Sarkaria Commission could be selectively used for political gains when it had not found anyone guilty of corruption? and why Vijay had chosen to refer to late leaders such as Murasoli Maran?With no response forthcoming from either the treasury benches or the speaker, DMK intensified its protest.The situation turned chaotic after speaker Prabhakar ruled that there was “no need to expunge the CM’s remarks”. He said Vijay had merely referred to the Sarkaria Commission, whose findings had been discussed in the House earlier, and that the CM’s speech was within the rules of the assembly.The ruling triggered a fresh round of protests, with DMK MLAs raising slogans and sitting in the well, keeping the moments tense for nearly 45 minutes, starting from 9.31am and ending at about 10.11am. In between, the speaker also cautioned minister Aadhav Arjuna for his remarks that they would also match the opposition.The speaker repeatedly asked the members to return to their seats and offered to allow Velu and deputy leader of the opposition K N Nehru to speak on the issue. But the DMK members refused to relent.“I will not reverse my ruling,” Prabhakar asserted before directing marshals to remove the protesting MLAs. He cautioned Kallakurichi MLA Vasantham K Karthikeyan against approaching the Chair.Marshals entered the House at about 10.08am and physically removed several MLAs who refused to leave the well, including Kutty alias A Sudhakar of Valparai, Durai Chandrasekaran of Thiruvaiyaru and Vasantham Karthikeyan of Rishivandiyam.Later in the day, Chezhiaan moved a privilege motion against Vijay, accusing the CM of making “baseless allegations” and citing reports connected to cases pending before courts during his reply to the demands for grants for the home department.
Article Summary: Dramatic scenes unfolded after speaker J C D Prabhakar refused to expunge Vijay’s remarks. DMK members raised slogans and staged a sit-in protest on the well of the House. As the protesting members refused to return to their seats, the speaker ordered marshals to remove them.

Article Title: Delhi building collapse: SC appointed amicus curiae seeks safety audit of PGs, hostels across capital
Article Text:
6 killed in Satya Niketan building collapse; FIR against owner

NEW DELHI: A Supreme Court-appointed amicus curiae on Wednesday filed a report before the top court on the building collapse in Satya Niketan and requested the apex court to direct its appointed committee to carry out inspections and safety audits of all PG accommodations, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments situated in and around colleges and universities across Delhi.Senior advocate Ajit Kumar Sinha, in his report, said that the Satya Niketan incident assumes significance as the locality had witnessed another building collapse in April 2022, in which two people were killed and four injured.“The present incident is also required to be viewed in the context of an earlier building collapse in Satya Niketan in April 2022, in which two persons lost their lives, and four others were injured. The recurrence of such an incident in the same locality raises serious concerns regarding the effectiveness of the existing mechanism for inspection, identification of dangerous structures, and enforcement of building bye-laws”, the amicus report said.He also noted that construction-related work was being undertaken in or around the basement and that there were reports of waterlogging in the basement immediately before the latest collapse.The amicus has sought a time-bound inspection and safety audit of PGs, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments around colleges and universities across Delhi, including checks on sanctioned building plans, actual construction and number of floors, basement construction and alterations, land use, structural and fire safety, ingress and egress, and dangerous or ruinous conditions.This comes after seven people were killed when a building collapsed in Satya Niketan on Sunday.Meanwhile, Municipal Corporation of Delhi also directed its executive engineers (building) across all zones to inspect structures under their jurisdiction and submit comprehensive reports by September 10, following the deadly building collapse in south Delhi's Satya Niketan, which killed seven people, officials said.Officials said the information collected during the inspections would be incorporated into an affidavit to be filed before the Delhi High Court within 10 days.The inspections and submission of reports will be personally monitored and supervised by the additional commissioners concerned in each zone, according to the order, they added.
Article Summary: A Supreme Court-appointed amicus curiae filed a report before the top court on the building collapse in Satya Niketan. He requested the apex court to direct its appointed committee to carry out inspections and safety audits of all PG accommodations, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments situated in and around colleges and universities.

Senior White House officials have privately warned US President Donald Trump that the war with Iran could continue for the rest of his presidency, despite his public prediction that the conflict will end soon after this year’s midterm elections, The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio were among the advisers who reportedly raised the possibility during private discussions with Trump in the Oval Office and Situation Room.According to the report, the officials told Trump that Iran could continue resisting US pressure, potentially keeping the conflict going until after the next US presidential inauguration in January 2029.Trump has publicly offered a much shorter timeline for the conflict. Article Title: 'Get off our roads Mr Singh': Trump administration's 'self-deport' advertisement sparks row
Article Text:

A US department of homeland security (DHS) social media post targeting Indian Americans with the warning “self-deport or find out” has sparked an online backlash, with critics calling the campaign “racist” and “anti-Indian”.The AI-generated post, shared by the official DHS account on X amid the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown, uses characters from the Transformers franchise.It features Optimus Prime, the franchise’s protagonist, confronting a brown-bearded man, “Mr Singh” with the message: “Self-deport or find out”.The post also carries the message: “Get off our roads, you don’t know how to drive Mr Singh”, drawing further criticism over its reference to the common Indian and Sikh surname.The campaign is part of the administration’s broader crackdown on illegal immigration and immigrant truck drivers.A related video features Megatron, the franchise’s antagonist, seeking the release of truck drivers Harjinder Singh, Rajinder Kumar, Bekzhan Beishekeev, Akhror Bozorov and Jasveer Singh, who were involved in road accidents and other crimes.“If you approach this nation with hostile intent, know this.We will defend ourselves. We will defend Americanism. We will defend our home,” the DHS said in an X post.The use of “Mr Singh” in the campaign drew sharp criticism from advocacy groups, including the Hindu American Foundation (HAF) and Sikh Coalition.“‘Singhs’ are Hindu, they are Sikhs, they are American and they drive. Racist, un-American, anti-Indian profiling/trolling by @DHSgov should shock our nation’s collective conscience,” HAF said in a post on X.“This is a discriminatory post by a federal agency that is far beyond political messaging, and we welcome an investigation,” the foundation said, tagging Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K Dhillon and FBI Director Kash Patel.The Sikh Coalition also criticised the campaign, saying Sikhs continue to face profiling based on their appearance.“Twenty-five years after 9/11, Sikhs are still being targeted and profiled for how we look,” the organisation said, news agency PTI reported.“Millions of Sikhs in the United States have the last name Singh, which means lion. We remain fearless in identifying as Sikhs – even when our government portrays us as enemies,” it added.The controversy comes as the DHS promotes its CBP Home programme, which allows eligible undocumented migrants to register their intention to voluntarily leave the United States.Migrants who register for self-deportation can receive travel assistance and an exit bonus of $2,600, according to the DHS.The campaign's focus on commercial drivers comes amid a broader US crackdown on undocumented migrants working in the trucking industry.
Article Summary: The AI-generated post was shared by the official DHS account on X. It features Optimus Prime, the franchise’s protagonist, confronting a brown-bearded man. The post also carries the message: “Get off our roads, you don’t know how to drive Mr Singh” The use of “Mr Singh’ in the campaign drew sharp criticism.

Article Title: ‘Quit politics completely’: Mayawati’s message to Ashok Siddharth as Akash Anand awaits big BSP role ahead of 2027 UP polls
Article Text:

What happened on September 3

The reshuffle around him

LUCKNOW: BSP national president Mayawati said on Tuesday that Ashok Siddharth, the father-in-law of her nephew Akash Anand, should take complete "sanyas" from politics. Only then, she said, would it be appropriate for Akash Anand to work freely in the party again.Akash Anand was the BSP's national convener until September 3, when Mayawati announced at an all-India meeting of party office-bearers that he would work as an ordinary party worker. She said it would not be appropriate to give him any major responsibility, adding that he still needed to become more "mature."Mayawati said on Tuesday that the party leadership will consider giving Akash Anand's responsibilities back to him only after Ashok Siddharth gives up politics completely.Ashok Siddharth, a former Rajya Sabha MP of the party, was expelled by Mayawati on August 2 for alleged anti-party activities.At the September 3 meeting, Mayawati told BSP office-bearers: "I have allowed Akash Anand to work in the party, which is before all of you, but Akash Anand still needs to become more mature. Till then, it would not be appropriate to give him a major responsibility in the party."She said Akash Anand, as national coordinator, would continue to work in the party. Mayawati invoked BSP founder Kanshi Ram's approach of allowing family members to assist with party work but opposing giving them election tickets or positions after the party came to power. "I am also completely committed to that resolve," she said.At the same meeting, Mayawati announced that the BSP has decided to contest all elections across the country on its own, without alliances. She also described the Congress as "strongly anti-Dalit and anti-Ambedkar" and criticised the RSS, citing recent remarks by its chief Mohan Bhagwat during his US visit.Both Akash Anand and Ishan Anand, Mayawati's younger nephew, attended the September 3 meeting.In the same period, Mayawati has brought back several previously expelled leaders into the party fold.Former national coordinator Randhir Singh Beniwal, expelled in August for alleged anti-party activities and indiscipline, has rejoined the BSP and been assigned as central coordinator responsible for organising the party in selected states. Senior leader Ashok Siddharth was removed at the same time as Beniwal but remains outside the party.Dharamveer Ashok, a former minister in the Mayawati-led UP government in 2007 and a former member of the legislative council, was expelled in April on similar charges and was readmitted in August.Meerut-based leaders Mohit Anand and Nitin Singh have also been named central coordinators. Singh was expelled last year and reinstated a few months later.Party sources said Mayawati is expanding the BSP's organisation at the national and state levels, with several returning leaders appointed as central coordinators to build cadres, oversee outreach, and strengthen the party's footprint in their allotted states.Mayawati has also dropped hints that she may appoint Ishan Anand, her younger nephew, as in charge of Sector-1 and Sector-2 in the party organisation, according to sources aware of a late-night meeting of national-level office-bearers held at her residence. No official announcement has been made.Sector-1 and Sector-2 cover all state units except Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand, which remain under Mayawati's direct supervision. If confirmed, the role would be Ishan Anand's first formal responsibility in the BSP.Ishan Anand, 27, is a graduate in legal studies from the University of Westminster in the UK. He made his first public appearance on the party stage on January 15, 2025, during Mayawati's birthday event, and attended a state-level meeting of the BSP's UP unit the next day — seen at the time as a signal of his growing involvement ahead of the 2027 assembly elections.The developments come ahead of the 2027 Punjab assembly election and the subsequent Uttar Pradesh assembly election. On August 25, Mayawati announced that the BSP would contest the Punjab polls "alone without any alliance or compromise with anyone," saying electoral tie-ups risked weakening the party's vote share and demoralising its cadre.The decision is significant for the BSP in Punjab, where founder Kanshi Ram began his political journey and where Scheduled Castes account for 31.94% of the population — the highest proportion of any state, according to the 2011 Census. Uttar Pradesh has the highest SC population in absolute numbers, at over 4.13 crore.
Article Summary: BSP national president Mayawati said on Tuesday that Ashok Siddharth, the father-in-law of her nephew Akash Anand, should take complete "sanyas" from politics. She said it would not be appropriate to give him any major responsibility, adding that he still needed to become more "mature" The BSP has decided to contest all elections across the country on its own, without alliances.

Article Title: ‘Bunch of liars’: Allahabad HC raps UP cops over illegal detention
Article Text:
The Allahabad High Court criticized Deoria police officials for alleged illegal detention





PRAYAGRAJ: Allahabad high court on Wednesday rapped the police chief of UP’s Deoria district and an SHO in a case of alleged ‘illegal detention’ of four persons and irked over the absence of CCTV footage in the case, calling them a ‘bunch of liars’.A bench of Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Divesh Chandra Samant expressed its disappointment with police officials over their explanation regarding the CCTV cameras, the alleged breakdown of the system, and the missing recordings for the period of the alleged detention — April 13-23, 2026.The court also directed UP govt to pay Rs 65,000 to the four petitioners, directing that the amount would be recovered from the salary of the SHO concerned.The bench was hearing a Habeas Corpus petition alleging that the four petitioners were unlawfully detained at the Gauri bazaar Police Station in Deoria.The court had directed the police to produce the CCTV recordings from inside the police station to verify the allegations made in the petitions but the SHO said that the same was not available as there was a technical fault in the system on the said dates.The court also questioned the SHO about whether any General Diary entry had been made regarding the repair of the CCTV system but he replied in the negative.Deoria SP stated that he had not been informed that the CCTV system was not functioning.The court expressed disappointment over the explanation and termed them a ‘bunch of liars’. ‘’Apologise to the people not to court,’’ the bench said when Deoria SP tendered an apology.The bench asked the SP about the action taken against the SHO, including whether he had been suspended or his service terminated. Justice Sreedharan orally remarked thus: “Did you suspend him, terminate him? An SHO of a Thana who cannot make a GD inquiry must be terminated. He is not fit to be a constable.”The bench further questioned the SP why no action was taken against the SHO after allegedly finding him guilty. The SP replied that the SHO had been sent to the Crime Branch but the bench was not satisfied with this action.The court also noted that the affidavit referred to the Supreme Court’s mandatory requirement requiring CCTV coverage at police stations and stated that the State Govt had released over Rs 46 lakh for police stations in Deoria district. However, the affidavit did not disclose the date on which the amount was released.The court termed the date of release “essential and vital” and noted that the further actions attributed to the SP were dated Aug 14, 2026, after the High Court’s Aug 4 order. The bench observed: “Prima facie, it appears that the district authorities have initiated action only as a response to the petition being filed before this court and the order dated Aug 4, 2026.”The bench also questioned the authorities regarding the payment made to the agency responsible for the CCTV system. The court questioned why the entire amount had been released despite the work allegedly not having been completed. It remarked thus: “Instead of blacklisting them, you released the entire fund. On the basis of assurance, you released the entire amount.”
Article Summary: Allahabad High Court criticized Deoria police officials for alleged illegal detention of four petitioners. A bench of Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Divesh Chandra Samant expressed its disappointment with police officials over their explanation. The court also directed UP govt to pay Rs 65,000 to the four petitioner, directing that the amount would be recovered from the salary of the SHO concerned.
