Article Text:
A woman allegedly orchestrated her father-in-law's murder while attending a party with her husband.

Murder allegedly planned over CCTV cameras

Plan was to make murder look like heart attack

Nothing stolen from house





KANPUR: A woman accused of masterminding the murder of her 63-year-old father-in-law was allegedly dancing at a lounge with her husband around the same time the killing was taking place, with police now claiming she remained in contact with the alleged assailants during the crime.A video of Shalu Minocha dancing at a lounge in Kanpur on the night her father-in-law, Vineet Minocha, was murdered surfaced on social media on Wednesday and went viral. Police said the footage, recorded by lounge staff, confirms that Shalu and her husband Subrat were at Cosmozin Lounge in Tilak Nagar that night.Also read: 3 plans. 1 target. 26 stabs: 'Killer bahu’s’ chilling murder script According to investigators, however, Shalu allegedly stayed in touch with the men she had hired to kill Vineet through WhatsApp calls, messages and voice calls and even guided them while she was at the party.The lounge's CCTV DVR was found to have no stored footage, but videos recorded by the staff showed around 20-25 people, mostly couples, dancing to Bollywood songs. Shalu was seen wearing a dark purple gown while her husband was dressed in a grey shirt.In one of the videos, the couple is seen dancing to the song Tum To Dhokhebaaz Ho, Vaada Karke Bhool Jaate Ho. Police said nothing about Shalu's behaviour appeared unusual and other guests at the lounge seemed unaware of what was allegedly unfolding at her home.Police arrested Shalu on Monday, alleging that she had masterminded the murder of her father-in-law after a former employee of Vineet claimed she had offered him Rs 6 lakh for the killing.Investigators suspect the alleged murder was linked to a dispute over CCTV cameras that Vineet had installed inside their apartment about 15-20 days before his death. Police said Shalu objected to the cameras, claiming they violated her privacy and caused her emotional distress.According to police, Shalu approached Vishal Gautam, a former employee at Vineet's pharmaceutical store, and allegedly gave him the original key to the family's apartment so that a duplicate could be made.Vishal then allegedly roped in his unemployed acquaintance Raj Kishor, 30, promising him an advance of Rs 30,000.Police said that on September 5, Shalu informed the accused that she, her husband and their son would be attending a party. She allegedly facilitated their entry into Ratan Orbit Apartment in Kalyanpur despite initial resistance from the security guard.The duo allegedly told the guard that they were delivering medicines, with Vishal registering himself under the fictitious name Shivam.According to investigators, Vishal and Raj hid inside a bedroom after entering the apartment using the duplicate key.Police said Shalu had allegedly instructed them to suffocate Vineet with a pillow so that his death would appear to be from a heart attack.The plan allegedly went awry when Vineet entered the bedroom around 11pm and noticed something unusual.DCP West SM Qasim Abidi said the two men panicked and allegedly attacked Vineet with knives before fleeing the apartment by jumping over the rear wall.The postmortem later revealed 26 stab wounds on Vineet's body.Police said the murder took place sometime between 10.30pm on Saturday and 3am on Sunday while Vineet was alone in the four-room apartment.Shalu and Subrat returned from the party and found Vineet's bloodied body before alerting police.Investigators said CCTV footage showed Vishal and Raj leaving the apartment after the murder. They were arrested following an encounter late Sunday.After receiving medical treatment, Vishal allegedly told police that he had killed Vineet on Shalu's instructions in return for money.Police said nothing was stolen from the apartment, strengthening their suspicion that the killing was motivated by personal enmity rather than robbery. Section 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, relating to criminal conspiracy, has also been added to the case.Police said Shalu allegedly admitted her involvement in the presence of female police personnel after being confronted with Vishal.The investigation is continuing, with police examining the alleged communications between Shalu and the assailants as well as the circumstances surrounding the murder.
Article Summary: Video of Shalu Minocha dancing at a lounge on the night her father-in-law was murdered surfaced on social media on Wednesday and went viral. Police said the footage, recorded by lounge staff, confirms that Shalu and her husband Subrat were at Cosmozin Lounge in Tilak Nagar that night.

Article Title: ‘I’m not special human, cannot work 24X7’: Varanasi cop resigns
Article Text:
A Varanasi police constable resigned citing inability to work round the clock.





LUCKNOW: A police constable posted at Ramnagar police station in Varanasi sparked concern among senior officers after he posted a resignation letter in the station’s official WhatsApp group, saying he did not possess “special human powers” to work round the clock.Constable Devgan Kumar Chauhan posted the letter on the evening of Sept 7, requesting that he be relieved from service. The unusual wording of the resignation immediately drew the attention of senior police officials, who summoned both the station house officer and the constable to ascertain the circumstances behind the move.In the letter addressed to the police commissioner, Chauhan wrote, “I am currently not capable of working 24x7 every day. Since I do not possess the powers of any special human, I request you to relieve me from my duties.”According to police officials, the constable had been under mental stress after being repeatedly assigned duty with a patient undergoing treatment at a trauma centre for several days. He was also reportedly facing personal problems at home.The constable also raised concerns over the manner in which duties were being assigned at the police station.He accused a head constable, referred to as a diwan, of irregularities in duty allocation.Chauhan claimed that some personnel considered close to the head constable were given comparatively easier schedules or rest, while attempts were made to assign round-the-clock duties to other constables.His resignation letter subsequently became a talking point within the department, as it highlighted concerns surrounding prolonged duty hours and the mental pressure faced by police personnel.ACP Vijay Pratap Singh said the constable had gone home after completing his duty on the night of September 5 but was informed the following day that he would again have to accompany the patient.The officer said Chauhan was also facing difficulties due to domestic issues and appeared to have taken the decision to submit his resignation while under stress.“Later, during a phone conversation, he made it clear that he wanted to continue in service,” the ACP said.Following the intervention of senior officers, Chauhan was counselled, and his request for voluntary relief from service was not accepted. He has since indicated that he wants to continue working as a police constable.The resignation letter was subsequently deleted from the official group, but screenshots of the message have circulated widely on social media.The incident has once again brought attention to the demanding working conditions of police personnel, particularly long duty hours, continuous deployment and the need to address stress and mental well-being within the force.
Article Summary: Constable Devgan Kumar Chauhan posted the letter on the evening of Sept 7, requesting that he be relieved from service. Chauhan had been under mental stress after being repeatedly assigned duty with a patient undergoing treatment at a trauma centre for several days. He was also reportedly facing personal problems at home.

Article Title: Twist in influencer Manjeet Kaur murder: 1st arrest in case; accused claims she was set ablaze in Sector 34
Article Text:
According to the investigation, Manjeet was allegedly called to Sector 34 on the intervening night of July 3 and 4 by persons known to her (Image Credit: Instagram)





CHANDIGARH: A fortnight after social media influencer Manjeet Kaur succumbed to injuries she sustained after allegedly being kidnapped, tied to a tree and set ablaze near Morinda, Chandigarh Police made the first arrest in the case on Tuesday.The accused, Parminder Singh alias Pinda, a resident of Kapurthala, was arrested late Tuesday night near the Sector 38 motor market by a team from Sector 34 police station.Police produced Pinda before a court on Wednesday and secured a four-day police remand for further questioning.According to police, investigators established Pinda’s presence at the scene through call detail records and tower location data linked to Manjeet’s alleged kidnapping. During interrogation, Pinda allegedly admitted his involvement in the kidnapping but denied any role in setting her on fire.According to the preliminary investigation, Manjeet was allegedly called to Sector 34 on the intervening night of July 3 and 4 by persons known to her. She was allegedly assaulted, forced into a vehicle and taken to a forested area near Morinda in Punjab, where she was tied to a tree and set ablaze.Police said another acquaintance who reached the spot later managed to douse the flames with a blanket. Manjeet was initially taken to a hospital in Morinda before being shifted to a private hospital in Mohali. She was later admitted to PGI, Chandigarh, where she remained under treatment until her death on Aug 26.Police are treating the matter as a “double murder” case as Manjeet was allegedly around seven weeks pregnant at the time of her death.According to investigators, Pinda claimed Manjeet had told him the unborn child was his, a claim he denied. Police are probing the dispute over the pregnancy as a possible motive behind the crime.Manjeet’s mother had earlier expressed suspicion against Pinda and Rinku, another acquaintance of the victim, and both were named in the FIR. Police are also investigating whether the accused attempted to exploit an existing social media rivalry involving one of Manjeet’s acquaintances to mislead investigators and create a false trail.Further investigation is underway, and police are questioning Pinda to establish the sequence of events and determine the roles of other suspects.According to police sources, Pinda claimed during interrogation that Manjeet was not taken to the Morinda forest area and was instead set on fire behind a park in Sector 34 following an argument with Rinku.Sources said the dispute allegedly escalated into a physical altercation, after which Manjeet was taken in a car, assaulted and set ablaze. However, the flames were allegedly extinguished later when the accused feared the consequences. Rinku then allegedly took her to a flat in Kharar, believing she might survive.Police, however, said Pinda’s version cannot be treated as conclusive, as he is the first accused to be arrested in the case and his claims are being independently verified.
Article Summary: Manjeet Kaur succumbed to injuries she sustained after allegedly being kidnapped, tied to a tree and set ablaze near Morinda. Chandigarh Police made the first arrest in the case on Tuesday. Parminder Singh alias Pinda, a resident of Kapurthala, was arrested late Tuesday night near the Sector 38 motor market by a team from Sector 34 police station.

Article Title: Ashok Siddharth takes ‘sanyas’ from politics after Mayawati says his retirement can save Akash Anand’s future
Article Text:
Ashok Siddharth, an expelled BSP leader, has announced his retirement from politics.





LUCKNOW: Expelled BSP leader, Ashok Siddharth, on Thursday, said that he is taking 'sanyas' from politics. He is a former Rajya Sabha MP of BSP, and father-in-law of BSP national president Mayawati 's nephew, Akash Anand.Mayawati, on Wednesday, had said that if Ashok Siddharth retires from politics completely, it will be good for Akash Anand's political career in the party, and that he will be able to work freely in the party.On Thursday, Ashok Siddharth, in his long post on X, said, "For me, your command is the greatest. My relationships, family, everything feels utterly insignificant in front of it. Under your guidance, for the past thirty-five years, I have been devoted to the BSP and its mission . Whatever responsibilities you have entrusted to me thus far, I have strived to fulfill them with all my might. You are my political guru, my elder sister. It is because of you that I have had the privilege of serving as a member of the Legislative Council and the Rajya Sabha. You deemed someone as ordinary as me worthy enough to make a mere worker like me a part of your family. This is a debt I can never repay in this lifetime. "He also clarified that he never did anything against the interests of the party, or Mayawati.On him having an influence over Akash Anand, he added, "Let alone advising Akash Ji, I haven't even met him in the past several months except on a couple of occasions when his programs were scheduled in those states for which you had assigned me the responsibility."He also pointed out that there were people within the party who have been accusing him of trying to seize control of the party, of attempting to mislead Akash Anand, out of envy. "This is a conspiracy by my political opponents, who are themselves engaged in anti-party activities, and the truth of which will surely come before you one day or another. "He also urged Mayawati to not link his "sanyas" with Akash's return to the party, or his growth in the party. "He is your nephew before being my son-in-law. He has your blood running in his veins; he has spent two decades of his life under your shelter and care, how could an ordinary worker like me possibly mislead him? You understand his good and bad better than anyone else; whether to give him responsibility again or not is your decision," said Ashok Siddharth.He continued to request that by linking his retirement from politics to Akash Anand's career in the party, an ordinary worker like him is being given more importance than he deserves.Mayawati had recently restricted the role of Akash Anand in the party, and had allowed him to work only as an ordinary party worker. Akash Anand was the national convener of the party till Mayawati limited his role in the party.In her post, on Wednesday, she had blamed Ashok Siddharth for Akash Anand's fall in the party.
Article Summary: Expelled BSP leader, Ashok Siddharth, on Thursday, said that he is taking'sanyas' from politics. He is a former Rajya Sabha MP, and father-in-law of BSP national president Mayawati's nephew, Akash Anand.

Article Title: Satya Niketan building collapse: PG operator ran 7 such facilities in same area
Article Text:
The operator, Shudhanshu Lovneesh told cops he and associate Shubham Tyagi had leased four floors of the building in August last year for Rs 1.05 lakh a month.

PG operator fled after students identified him





NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has arrested the man who used to run a PG facility on four floors of the building that collapsed in Satya Niketan under the name Hostel Daze.Police suspect he runs a total of seven such facilities in the area under the same name and are probing his entire operation. This building collapsed on Sept 6, leaving seven people dead.The operator, Shudhanshu Lovneesh (31) has told cops that he had taken four floors in the ill-fated building on lease, along with associate Shubham Tyagi, in Aug last year for Rs 1.05 lakh per month. Tyagi is absconding.They managed to rent the building cheap due to its dilapidated condition.A resident of Bhajanpura, Lovneesh graduated from Delhi University in 2019, and three years later, in 2022, he and Tyagi got into the business of running PG accommodations in Satya Niketan. He has told the cops that there are several others like him who are operating such facilities in old buildings on lease.A Delhi court Wednesday remanded Lovneesh and two others - building owner's son Mahesh Gupta (52) and contractor Sanoj - in two days in police custody. Mahesh was produced after his earlier two-day police remand ended. Police had sought three days' custody for all three to question them and confront them with the owner of the building, Hariram Gupta (81) who retired from IAF, and his wife, Urmila (75) who had been sent to 14 days in judicial custody Monday.Contractor Sanoj has told the cops that the basement was getting flooded with rainwater for 8 to 10 days and, in an unconventional solution, had been filled with three truckloads of construction debris to bring it up to the level of the ground floor.Police Wednesday confirmed TOI's report that the building collapsed like a pack of cards because a retaining wall on the ground floor was removed to merge two shops. Four additional floors had already been built on a weak foundation and the removal of the wall was the last straw.Sanoj told the police that he had been engaged for the work by Mahesh Gupta around 10 days before the incident and was being paid Rs 2,800 per day. He had been apprehended from Kasganj in UP on Tuesday. The labourers engaged in the work were being paid Rs 800 daily and they too are being questioned.Police sources said Lovneesh had reached the spot soon after the building collapsed but fled after students began to point him out as the operator of the PG. He then rushed to a friend's house in Burari, from where the police have nabbed him.The proceedings for remand of Lovneesh, Mahesh Gupta and Sanoj in the court of judicial magistrate Kautuk Bharadwaj were held in camera after the counsel for Lovneesh said the case was at a nascent stage and a "media trial" would prejudice the ongoing probe. The magistrate then directed the media personnel to leave the courtroom.
Article Summary: Police suspect he runs a total of seven such facilities in the area under the same name. The operator, Shudhanshu Lovneesh (31) has told cops that he had taken four floors in the ill-fated building on lease, along with associate Shubham Tyagi, in Aug last year for Rs 1.05 lakh per month. Tyagi is absconding.

Article Title: Enforcement Directorate: ED searches minister Jarkiholi, daughter over sugar, Africa biz deals
Article Text:
ED raids Karnataka PWD Minister Satish Jarkiholi, his daughter's residences among 18 places in money laundering case





BENGALURU/BELAGAVI: Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Wednesday carried out simultaneous searches at 18 premises linked to Karnataka PWD minister Satish Jarkiholi , his daughter and Chikkodi MP Priyanka Jarkiholi, and their associates across Karnataka and neighbouring Maharashtra.The multi-city crackdown was a fresh investigation, reportedly under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) and not linked to any ongoing money-laundering case involving Manjunath.Belagavi district, home turf of the Jarkiholi family, served as a major focal point of the ED searches, with officials deployed at seven key locations across Belagavi city and Gokak taluk.Simultaneous searches were also conducted at the 64-year-old minister’s residence in Dollars’ Colony and his official quarters on Crescent Road in Bengaluru. While minister Satish Jarkiholi was at his Bengaluru residence, his daughter Priyanka was in Belagavi.Investigators are scrutinising foreign exchange flows allegedly linked to sugar industries, mining ventures and commercial projects in African countries, particularly Rwanda and Uganda.ED teams arrived early in the morning at the minister’s primary family residence, where Priyanka was present during the operation.Officials also searched the Gokak premises of Vitthal Parasannavar and Raju Dharnatti, both known close aides of the minister.In Belagavi city, the teams searched the Laxmi Tekdi residence and Club Road office of Dr Girish Sonwalkar, as well as the Kumaraswamy Layout residence of former KPCC member Malagouda Patil.ED teams also searched, for the second time, the residence of Y Manjunath, the minister’s brother-in-law and an additional commissioner in the excise department.ED sources clarified that while earlier probes involving the state excise department had focused on family members, the present action is an independent investigation tracing suspected money trails linked to overseas entities.The searches triggered a political backlash in Karnataka, with Congress leaders alleging that central agencies were being used to target the state govt and its leaders.Defending his brother, MLC Lakhan Jarkiholi said Satish had several independent business interests, including sugar mills and overseas ventures, and would cooperate fully with the investigation and provide documents to establish the legitimacy of his assets and business dealings.
Article Summary: Karnataka PWD Minister Satish Jarkiholi, his daughter's residences among 18 places in money laundering case. Investigators are scrutinising foreign exchange flows allegedly linked to sugar industries, mining ventures and commercial projects in African countries, particularly Rwanda and Uganda.

Article Title: Teacher 'forced' me to recite 'will study Hindi': JNU student
Article Text:
The MA second-year student from Karnataka alleged the teacher mocked her accent and difficulty with Hindi words, and encouraged classmates to laugh at her.





NEW DELHI: A JNU student from a non-Hindi-speaking state has alleged her faculty member at Centre for Japanese Studies made her repeat the sentence "I will try my best to study Hindi" several times in front of her classmates as a form of punishment for not being able to comprehend the language, leading to a "panic attack".A complaint was submitted to the dean of School of Language, Literature and Cultural Studies Shoba Sivasankaran on Sept 8. There was no immediate response from either her or the faculty member.The MA second-year student from Karnataka, who belongs to SC category, alleged the teacher mocked her accent and difficulty with Hindi words, and encouraged classmates to laugh at her.She alleged she had been subjected to such behaviour since the beginning of her programme, creating "an increasingly distressing and intimidating classroom environment". "In recent months, I have experienced severe anxiety, nausea, fear and panic-like symptoms before and during the class," the complaint stated.She decided to file the complaint after a recent incident on Sept 1, when a confrontation with the professor over her attendance led to her breaking down. "When I returned to class on Sept 1, the teacher interrogated me in front of the class for missing lectures. I responded, 'I was sick for two weeks, and I am still sick.'He then asked why I had not submitted an application letter to the office," she alleged. She claimed he accused her of "showing attitude" and disturbing the class, and eventually told her to either stop or leave. "By that stage, I was extremely distressed. I responded by saying, 'You have been terrorising us,' and left the classroom," she stated. The professor then allegedly refused to take classes.The student has sought measures to prevent further "public humiliation, linguistic targeting and intimidation".
Article Summary: A complaint was submitted to the dean of School of Language, Literature and Cultural Studies. The MA second-year student from Karnataka alleged the teacher mocked her accent and difficulty with Hindi words. The student has sought measures to prevent further "public humiliation, linguistic targeting and intimidation"

Article Title: ‘Lal Mandir was original target’: How traffic forced Red Fort bomber to change plans
Article Text:
The National Investigation Agency filed a charge sheet detailing the Red Fort vehicle-borne IED attack.

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think can help prevent attacks in crowded public places? Stronger security measures Better surveillance and monitoring Public awareness and vigilance 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: On Nov 10 last year, 13 minutes before the explosive-laden i20 exploded near Red Fort, bomber Umar-un-Nabi tried to park the car near ‘Lal Mandir’ in Chandni Chowk — suggesting it was the first target — but was diverted due to heavy traffic and police presence there. CCTV footage captured him attempting to park at 6.37pm, after which he took a U-turn and reached near Gate No. 4 of Red Fort, where he triggered the IED at 6.50pm.The details are part of the chargesheet recently filed by National Investigation Agency (NIA) in connection with the Red Fort blast. The chargesheet provides extensive details of the planning and execution of the first-ever vehicle-borne IED (VBIED) attack reported in the national capital.NIA has said the VBIED was detonated through a remote ‘command mechanism’ fitted in one of the shoes of the bomber, Umar-un-Nabi. A metal piece attached to the heel of one shoe was found adjacent to the i20 used by Umar, and it tested positive for triacetone triperoxide (TATP), potassium and ammonium nitrate. The other exhibits from this car included a nasal orifice swab matched with the DNA of Umar’s parents, confirming his identity as the bomber, the chargesheet stated.Further, a forensic report of the blast reported in Nowgam, J&K, on the explosives seized from Umar’s associates from Faridabad also tested positive for the same chemicals, confirming the module’s existence.“The yield (impact) of TATP and its stability also depends on its storage in a cold environment and presence of 10% water. Witnesses have deposed that Umar used to keep his room extremely cool, and that a foul smell used to emanate from it. He and others had also purchased collapsible water bags, which were used to keep the prepared TATP under wet conditions to keep it safe. Water was regularly added to the IED to keep the explosive mixture stable,” the chargesheet said.The post-mortem reports of the victims furnished by the hospital ascertain the cause of death to be “high-intensity blast wave effect”. The blast, the chargesheet said, led to the death of 11 people and injuries to 29. Damage to the nearby structures amounted to Rs 17.7 lakh, as assessed by authorities like DMRC, ASI and PWD, it added.NIA found that on Oct 30, Umar met an acquaintance behind Al Falah hospital, gave him his room key and asked him to bring his “shoes” from the almirah in the room. “He was already wearing his shoes at the time. He was visibly distressed as J&K police had raided the module by then,” said the chargesheet.While on the run, Umar was storing his urine in a polythene bag, as observed by the woman who owned the house in Nuh where he had sought shelter. “He did not go outside to dispose of it and thus a foul smell was emanating from the room, prompting the woman to complain to her husband,” the chargesheet said.“Interestingly, an innovative method for preparing explosive substances using urea nitrate has been elaborated in a PDF material seized from the pen drives of the accused wherein an alternative method for the source of urea is mentioned as — ‘extracting urea from urine’.”It also mentioned the seizure of a terror manual, “Lone Mujahid Pocket Book”, which was published in “Inspire” magazine, affiliated with Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP), being followed by the module. NIA said the manual provided operational information related to explosives, weapons, vehicles, arson and covert activities, with detailed chapters on TATP and remote-control mechanisms for detonating IEDs.On Nov 7, Umar also bought a new T-shirt, a wine-coloured shirt and green-coloured cargo pants by making payment in cash to a shop in Nuh, the chargesheet said.
Article Summary: NIA has said the VBIED was detonated through a remote ‘command mechanism’ fitted in one of the shoes of the bomber, Umar-un-Nabi. A metal piece attached to the heel of one shoe was found adjacent to the i20 used by Umar.

Article Title: Gaurav Bhatia defamation case: Delhi HC asks CJP members if they will voluntarily take down posts
Article Text:
The court observed that there were different ways to protest and that criticism should be expressed in a more articulate manner.

(With agency inputs)





NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Thursday asked the defendants in a defamation case filed by senior advocate and BJP leader Gaurav Bhatia whether they were willing to voluntarily remove the disputed social media posts.The court observed that there were different ways to protest and that criticism should be expressed in a more articulate manner.Justice Tushar Rao Gedela made the observations while hearing Bhatia’s Rs 2-crore defamation suit against Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Abhijeet Dipke and others. Bhatia appeared in person, according to news agency ANI.During the hearing, the court questioned the inclusion of Abhijeet Dipke as a defendant and asked what material had been posted by him. Counsel for Dipke submitted that there was not a single tweet by him forming the subject matter of the dispute and that the prayers in the suit were essentially against defendants Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka.The court observed that there appeared to be "nothing against him" and indicated that Dipke could be removed as a party.The court also asked counsel appearing for the other defendants to take instructions on whether they were willing to voluntarily remove the disputed posts."There are different ways of protesting. You are all youngsters. You may have anxieties. But attacking like this without verifying is not correct," the court observed.The court said it did not want to pass a takedown order at this stage if the defendants were willing to remove the content on their own.Counsel for Das submitted that the tweet in question had already been deleted.The court, however, pointed out that another post had also been put up. "You have the right to express, but sometimes expressions need to be put in a more articulate manner, so that intention goes in the right way," the court observed.The judge also told Bhatia that there could be other ways of addressing the issue and observed that he could have approached the defendants before moving the court.Bhatia submitted that the case involved aggravated defamation and argued that the disputed posts should not remain online as the defendants had a large number of followers. He said the posts were damaging his reputation and that he had given the defendants an opportunity to remove the content.Bhatia further alleged that his photograph had been used alongside a fabricated statement and that the logo of a news agency had been included in the graphic, giving the content an appearance of credibility.The court questioned Bhatia about how Dipke and the CJP had been made parties to the proceedings and what specific acts were attributed to them.Bhatia said the suit copy had also been served on X.The court reiterated that defendants Nos. 1 and 2, namely Das and Ranka, were the persons against whom the immediate allegations had been made and asked them to take instructions.The court further advised the young defendants that they had many things ahead of them, including studies and other work, and questioned why they should spend their time litigating in court.The matter was thereafter passed over, with the defendants being asked to take instructions and return to the court.Bhatia has filed the suit seeking Rs 2 crore in damages, along with permanent and mandatory injunctions, over allegedly defamatory content circulated on social media platform X.According to the plaint, the immediate dispute relates to an AI-generated graphic which allegedly carried Bhatia's photograph and attributed remarks concerning Swatantra Bhardwaj to him.Bhatia has denied making the alleged remarks. The plaint states that the disputed post was viewed by more than 1.32 lakh people and was subsequently deleted after Bhatia objected to it.The suit alleges that Das and Ranka published or amplified the disputed material and that Bhatia’s photograph was used alongside the alleged statement, creating a false impression that he was its source. Bhatia has claimed that the circulation of the content caused reputational damage.
Article Summary: The court observed that there were different ways to protest and that criticism should be expressed in a more articulate manner. Justice Tushar Rao Gedela made the observations while hearing Bhatia’s Rs 2-crore defamation suit against Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Abhijeet Dipke and others.
